title: Daily Market Digest: August 17, 2026
subtitle: Market futures show mixed sentiment as investors weigh inflation data and upcoming retail earnings.

items.headline: U.S. Futures Show Mixed Opening; Diminished Fed Rate Hike Odds Support Broader Market
items.summary: U.S. stock futures are indicating a mixed start to the trading week, as investors digest softer inflation and retail sales data from last week which has reduced the likelihood of a Federal Reserve rate hike in September. The sentiment is generally positive, continuing a bullish run driven by strong AI infrastructure earnings and cooling inflation, despite recent tepid retail spending figures.

items.headline: July Retail Sales Decline and Soft Consumer Sentiment Weigh on Economic Outlook
items.summary: U.S. retail sales experienced a 0.6% decline in July, marking the first drop since April and missing expectations, indicating that consumers spent less last month. This data, coupled with a dip in the University of Michigan's preliminary August consumer sentiment reading to 51 from 55.2, suggests a potential slowdown in consumer spending and has further eased concerns about aggressive Federal Reserve tightening.

items.headline: FOMC Minutes and Key Economic Data Ahead This Week
items.summary: The highly anticipated minutes from the July Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting are slated for release on Wednesday, August 19. While expected to reflect a hawkish stance, recent softer U.S. economic data may make these minutes appear somewhat dated. No major U.S. economic data releases are scheduled for Monday or Tuesday, but Friday will bring the U.S. Purchasing Managers' Index for the services sector.

items.headline: Retail Giants Set to Report Earnings, Offering Insights into Consumer Health
items.summary: This week will see major retail companies report quarterly earnings, providing critical insights into the health of the American consumer. Walmart ($WMT) is scheduled for Thursday, while Target ($TGT) and Home Depot ($HD) will report on Wednesday and Tuesday, respectively. JPMorgan has been identified as a high-conviction setup ahead of these reports.

items.headline: AI Infrastructure and Energy Sectors Show Continued Strength
items.summary: The AI infrastructure sector continues its robust growth, with 'picks & shovels' industrial companies also benefiting from the demand. Last week saw AI infrastructure leaders Nebius ($NBIS) and CoreWeave ($CRWV) report significant earnings beats, driving substantial stock rallies. The energy sector also experienced upward movement amid ongoing geopolitical tensions, with institutional capital flowing into cash-rich operators.
